standard: Static analysis + route analysis + runtime registration analysis + scheduler/queue analysis + container resolution analysis + configuration analysis + test verification. Never 'grep returned zero'.

verification_layers.evidence: Route::getRoutes() - 442 controller actions enumerated; none referenced these classes.
Console kernel schedule() driven with a real Schedule instance - 4 entries (currency:sync-rates, inspire, rewards:expire, bookings:expire-pending). None referenced these classes.
Artisan::all() - 133 registered commands compared against each class.
All 62 models queried; none resolves to any policy.
Model inheritance checked so relation-discovered models are not misjudged.
Every varchar/text/char/json/longtext column in all 74 tables scanned for stored class names.
Full suite re-run after the deletion batch.

false_positives_caught.detail: The first detector matched class names against Artisan command SIGNATURES. 'ExpirePendingBookings' does not appear in 'bookings:expire-pending', so three running scheduled jobs were flagged dead. This is the exact failure mode Phase 0.13 documented, reproduced by a new detector and caught by runtime verification.
false_positives_caught.proof: routes/console.php + schedule:list + artisan list --raw all confirm the command is registered and scheduled (*/5 * * * *).

false_positives_caught.detail: Gate::getPolicyFor() returned it for the non-existent class string App\Models\Asset. No Asset model exists, so no model can ever resolve to it. Corrected in the opposite direction from the other false positives.

conclusion: 16 of 21 candidates deleted. 3 were live scheduled jobs, 2 were actively referenced, and 4 are unused models over live tables that are deliberately retained.
